assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and then observing the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state opened a whole class of quantum matter with protected boundary states. The idea is original, conceptually clean and has reshaped condensed-matter physics and materials design. This is a discovery in the sense of a prediction promptly realised in nature.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall proposal), and Molenkamp's group delivered the HgTe/CdTe observation after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Credit is fair with these three, but Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological-insulator discoveries (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Roy, Fu) sit near the boundary and are not on the supplied list, so the configuration is somewhat contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over roughly two decades in 2D and 3D systems; interpretation is stable and the field is mature. Recognition is, if anything, due.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be framed around the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or broader topological insulators, and who is then omitted.
My knowledge of the detailed priority sequence between theory groups is from memory and not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A nonzero theta-13 was the last unknown mixing angle and opened the way to leptonic CP-violation searches and the mass ordering. The measurement is a clear, discrete discovery with large consequences for the neutrino sector, following the 2015 prize for oscillations.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) reported reactor disappearance in 2012; Double Chooz, T2K and the earlier Chooz limits also contributed. The three names are a reasonable fit but the experimental-collaboration structure and the competing claims make a clean trio debatable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several reactor and accelerator experiments, with precision measurement continuing; interpretation is stable. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims from T2K and Double Chooz.
Whether the Committee views this as a step beyond the 2015 oscillation prize sufficient for a new award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached fractional uncertainty near 10^-18 and enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. A major instrumental discovery with direct fundamental-physics reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the first strontium clock; Ye drove the best performance and many-body clock advances. Two names are a clean pairing, though Hall, Hänsch, Wineland and others have earlier recognition and work on related ion clocks.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) reproduce results; maturing toward adoption by the metrology community. Timely.
uncertainties: Whether the redefinition of the second, still pending, would make recognition premature or better supported.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of magic-angle flat bands and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created moire quantum materials as a tunable platform for correlated physics. High originality and strong impact on the field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band; Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Cao et al.) observed the correlated states. This is a natural theory plus experiment trio, though the contribution of Cao, Fatemi and others on the experimental team and the broader moire community complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Observations replicated widely by many groups since 2018, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet settled; somewhat young.
uncertainties: Possibly premature relative to the length of the track record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy and led to the first source associations (TXS 0506+056, the Galactic plane). A clear, discovery-driven result in the spirit of the observational prizes.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is credited as the single driving figure of the IceCube concept; but this is a very large collaboration, and the Committee would have to reconcile one individual against many contributors (e.g. instrument leaders). A one-person prize is possible but needs more justification than the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed by independent analyses; source identification still limited to a few cases. Reasonably mature but astrophysical interpretation continues to develop.
uncertainties: Fairness of single-name credit for a collaboration of hundreds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum origin of primordial perturbations account for flatness, horizon uniformity and the near scale-invariant spectrum observed in the CMB. Intellectually central to modern cosmology, with Mukhanov's quantum-fluctuation calculation being the quantitative link to data.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde and Mukhanov are plausible, but Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Sato and Chibisov also made decisive contributions and are not on the supplied list; allocation of credit is clearly contested.
assessment.maturity: Predictions such as a nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum are well supported, but the inflationary mechanism itself, e.g. primordial gravitational waves, is not directly confirmed, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: No direct evidence for the inflaton or primordial B-modes.
Credit among five or more originators is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and Blatt's realisation established a leading platform for quantum computing. Significant and originating, though now broader than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal; Blatt's group provided early experimental implementation. Wineland and Monroe are also relevant, and Wineland is already a laureate, which affects the experimental side of the attribution.
assessment.maturity: Gate fidelities and scale are well demonstrated by several groups; the field is mature, but practical large-scale computing is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and the 2025 circuit-based prize.
Whether trapped-ion computing or optical-lattice simulation (B010) is the better framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's precision CMB maps fixed the cosmological parameters to percent level and established the standard Lambda-CDM model. Very high impact, though the discovery of the CMB anisotropies and the blackbody spectrum has already been recognised (2006, 2019).
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission; Spergel was central to the analysis and cosmological interpretation; Page led key instrument design and calibration. The credit is clear but the Committee may judge that the Nobel-level step was earlier or later (COBE, Planck).
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by Planck and other experiments; mature, with lasting impact.
uncertainties: Incremental to COBE and the 2019 prize in the Committee's eyes.
Large-team attribution is hard to reduce to three people.
